subject: pathology
title: Caseating and Non-Caseating Granulomas, Tuberculosis, and Sarcoidosis

steps.tx: Granulomas are broadly divided on histological grounds into two major diagnostic categories: necrotizing caseating granulomas and non-necrotizing non-caseating granulomas. The prototypical cause of caseating granulomatous disease is Mycobacterium tuberculosis, wherein infected centers undergo amorphous, cheesy, eosinophilic necrosis termed **caseating granulomatous inflammation**.
steps.say: Granulomas are classified as caseating or non-caseating based on the presence of central necrotic debris.

vis.caption: Caseating granuloma: caseous necrosis with Langhans giant cells. [Credit: StewardMD]
vis.alt: Caseating granuloma: caseous necrosis with Langhans giant cells.

steps.tx: In primary pulmonary tuberculosis, initial mycobacterial infection in mid-to-lower lung zones forms a localized subpleural caseating focus termed the Ghon focus. Combined with caseating hilar lymph node enlargement, this classical pairing represents the **Ghon primary complex**, which typically heals through dystrophic calcification to form a fibrocalcific Ranke complex.
steps.say: The Ghon primary complex pairs a subpleural caseating lung lesion with enlarged hilar lymph nodes.

nodes.label: Aerosolized Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Droplets Settle in Subpleural Alveoli
Macrophage Infiltration and Th1 Immunity Form 1-to-1.5 cm Ghon Focus
Organisms Drain via Lymphatics to Regional Hilar and Mediastinal Nodes
Ghon Complex Heals, Undergoing Fibrous Encapsulation and Calcification (Ranke)

steps.tx: Histological examination of tuberculous caseating granulomas reveals complete destruction of tissue architecture within the central core. Acid-fast bacilli are identified within the necrotic debris or phagocytosed inside epithelioid histiocytes using the **Ziehl-Neelsen carbolfuchsin stain**, appearing as slender, beaded, bright red rods under oil immersion.
steps.say: Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrates bright red, slender, acid-fast tuberculous bacilli within granulomas.

left.title: Caseating Granuloma Morphology
points: Central core: completely acellular, structureless, pink granular debris
Surrounding zone: palisaded rim of transformed epithelioid macrophages
Interspersed multinucleated Langhans giant cells with peripheral nuclei
Outer mantle: CD4+ T-lymphocytes, plasma cells, and fibrous collagen cuff

right.title: Non-Caseating Granuloma Morphology
points: Solid, non-necrotic aggregates of epithelioid macrophages throughout
Absence of central acellular caseous or liquefactive necrotic debris
Cohesive, sharply demarcated, round to oval microscopic nodules
Characteristic of sarcoidosis, Crohn disease, berylliosis, and foreign bodies

steps.tx: In contrast to tuberculosis, sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory disorder characterized by the widespread formation of non-caseating granulomas. Typically presenting with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and pulmonary reticular infiltrates, **sarcoid non-caseating granulomas** present as uniform, cohesive, naked granulomas with minimal peripheral lymphocytic cuffs.
steps.say: Sarcoidosis forms clean, non-caseating granulomas that characteristically involve hilar lymph nodes.

vis.caption: Compact non-caseating pulmonary sarcoid granulomas showing tightly packed epithelioid histiocytes.
vis.alt: Non-caseating sarcoid granuloma with compact epithelioid cells and multinucleated giants

steps.tx: Under light microscopy, the multinucleated giant cells in sarcoid granulomas frequently contain two distinctive morphological inclusions. These are **Schaumann bodies**, which are laminated concentric calcified basophilic proteinaceous concretions, and asteroid bodies, which are stellate, star-shaped eosinophilic crystalline inclusions embedded within the giant cell cytoplasm.
steps.say: Sarcoid giant cells often contain laminated Schaumann bodies and star-shaped asteroid bodies.

left.title: Schaumann Bodies (Conchoidal Bodies)
points: Concentric, laminated, basophilic round proteinaceous concretions
Composed of calcium salts, iron, and complex mucopolysaccharides
Located within cytoplasm of multinucleated giant cells
Present in 60-80% of sarcoidosis and berylliosis granulomas

right.title: Asteroid Bodies
points: Stellate, radiating, star-shaped, bright eosinophilic inclusions
Composed of compressed cytoskeletal vimentin and lipid bilayers
Enclosed within clear vacuoles inside giant cell cytoplasm
Characteristic of sarcoidosis, but not entirely pathognomonic

steps.tx: Leprosy (Hansen disease), caused by Mycobacterium leprae, exhibits a clinical and pathological spectrum dictated entirely by the host cell-mediated immune response. In patients with vigorous T-helper-one cell-mediated immunity, **tuberculoid leprosy** produces well-formed epithelioid granulomas that encircle and destroy cutaneous dermal nerves, with few acid-fast bacilli.
steps.say: Tuberculoid leprosy exhibits vigorous cell-mediated immunity, forming granulomas with rare bacilli.

vis.caption: Cutaneous lepromatous and tuberculoid leprosy lesions displaying altered host cell-mediated responses.
vis.alt: Cutaneous leprosy showing hypopigmented anesthetic plaques and nerve enlargement

steps.tx: Conversely, patients lacking effective T-cell immunity against Mycobacterium leprae develop lepromatous leprosy. Characterized by profound cell-mediated anergy, **lepromatous leprosy histology** reveals sheets of lipid-laden foamy macrophages termed Virchow cells packed with thousands of acid-fast bacilli arranged in bundles termed globi, producing facial lion-like leonine facies.
steps.say: Lepromatous leprosy lacks T-cell immunity, displaying foamy Virchow cells packed with globi of bacilli.

left.title: Tuberculoid Leprosy (High CMI)
points: Robust Th1 cell-mediated immunity with positive lepromin skin test
Well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells
Infiltrates and destroys peripheral dermal nerves, producing anesthesia
Paucibacillary: acid-fast bacilli are extremely rare or absent on biopsy

right.title: Lepromatous Leprosy (Low CMI)
points: Profound Th1 anergy with negative lepromin skin test; elevated Th2 cytokines
Absence of granulomas; sheets of foamy lipid-laden Virchow histiocytes
Multibacillary: packed with thousands of bacilli in parallel bundles (globi)
Produces leonine facies, loss of eyebrows, saddle nose, and testicular atrophy

steps.tx: In differentiating granulomatous diseases, detailed clinical history, microbiological stains, and special fungal cultures are essential. While caseous necrosis strongly favors tuberculosis, fungal histoplasmosis, or coccidioidomycosis, non-caseating granulomas warrant thorough clinical evaluation for sarcoidosis, Crohn disease, berylliosis, foreign body reactions, and **granulomatous polyangiitis**.
steps.say: Caseating granulomas indicate mycobacterial or fungal disease, while non-caseating indicate sarcoidosis or Crohn disease.
